column1:
Cautiously optimistic with a mild hawkish tilt. The FOMC emphasizes solid labor-market gains and views the Q1 growth slowdown as transitory, while noting inflation is near—though still somewhat below—its 2 percent objective. This stance is consistent with the Friedman-Phelps natural-rate view that there is no long-run inflation-unemployment trade-off and with the Fed’s credibility focus established since the Volcker era. The commitment to a symmetric 2 percent target and close monitoring of inflation expectations aligns with the inflation-forecast-targeting perspective (e.g., Svensson) and the central role of expectations in modern models. Keeping policy “gradual” reflects evidence that monetary tightening can depress future consumption growth (Canzoneri, Cumby, and Diba) and that policy has real effects (B. Friedman), supporting measured normalization while reinvestments maintain accommodative financial conditions. Low market-based inflation compensation suggests expectations remain contained, which, together with balanced risk assessment, supports a moderately positive tone rather than an outright hawkish one.
